Cycle-1 full pre-registration sweep: Ready - 0 blocking issues, 0 non-blocking hygiene issues, 0 suggestions.

Verdict: Ready for registration. The 17 staged rows are exactly the source-defined intersection of current AAU members and current Big Ten full members under the two cited master Wikipedia articles. Nebraska is correctly excluded, the 2024 expansion cohort is correctly included, and the Michigan 1896 joined-year choice is defensible because it follows the Big Ten article's primary joined-year value while documenting the 1907-1917 gap.

Findings:
- None.

Verification checks:
- Universe completeness: PASS. The Big Ten article states that the conference expanded to 18 member institutions on August 2, 2024 and that 17 current Big Ten universities are AAU members, except Nebraska (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, lead lines 287-289). The Big Ten full-member table lists 18 full members, including Nebraska (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, full members table lines 300-325). The AAU article's current-members table lists the staged Big Ten/AAU schools as current AAU members, and its former-members table lists `University of Nebraska–Lincoln` with AAU year joined 1909 and year left 2011 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, current members lines 255-307; former members lines 314-319). The CSV has 17 rows, which matches 18 Big Ten full members minus Nebraska.
- 2024 expansion: PASS. The Big Ten source lists Oregon joined 2024, UCLA joined 2024, USC joined 2024, and Washington joined 2024 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, full members table lines 314 and 320-324). The AAU source lists all four as current AAU members, with UCLA joined AAU 1974, Oregon 1969, USC 1969, and Washington 1950 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, current members lines 278, 296, 301, and 306).
- Michigan founding-member-with-gap edge case: PASS. The Big Ten table shows `University of Michigan` with joined values `1896 1917[d]`, and footnote d says Michigan was independent from 1907-08 to 1916-17 after being voted out in April 1907 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, full members table lines 307 and notes lines 327-330). Because the staged column is `Year Joined Big Ten` rather than `current continuous tenure start`, and because `1896` is the first/primary table value, staging `1896` is defensible. No suggestion to switch to `1917` is needed because the curation record explicitly documents the gap.
- Per-row spot checks: PASS. Indiana: Big Ten source gives Bloomington, Indiana, founded 1820, joined 1899; AAU gives Indiana University Bloomington, Indiana, established 1820, AAU joined 1909 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, lines 302-303; `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, line 255). Michigan State: Big Ten gives East Lansing, Michigan, founded 1855, joined 1950; AAU gives Michigan State University, Michigan, established 1855, AAU joined 1964 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, line 308; `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, line 259). Rutgers: Big Ten gives New Brunswick-Piscataway, New Jersey, founded 1766, joined 2014; AAU gives Rutgers University–New Brunswick, New Jersey, established 1766, AAU joined 1989 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, lines 318-319; `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, line 267). Maryland: Big Ten gives College Park, Maryland, founded 1856, joined 2014; AAU gives University of Maryland, College Park, Maryland, established 1856, AAU joined 1969 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, lines 305-306; `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, line 289). Wisconsin: Big Ten gives Wisconsin-Madison, Wisconsin, founded 1848, joined 1896; AAU gives University of Wisconsin–Madison, Wisconsin, established 1848, AAU joined 1900 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, line 325; `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, line 307).
- University name normalization: PASS. The staged names follow the AAU article's Institution column, including `Rutgers University–New Brunswick`, `University of Minnesota, Twin Cities`, `University of Maryland, College Park`, and `University of Wisconsin–Madison` (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities`, lines 267, 289, 292, and 307). This is a defensible source-priority rule where Big Ten link text uses slightly different display forms such as `University of Wisconsin-Madison` (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, line 325).
- Missing-source / Wiki-family discovery pass: PASS. The two cited master articles are the direct source pages for the two membership sets being intersected. The Big Ten article also contains an academics table that independently marks every current Big Ten school except Nebraska as an AAU member (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference`, lines 882-904), so no additional Wiki-family source is needed to define the row universe.
- Saturation milestone: PASS. Local cfg/staging scan shows 6 registered `set_operation` entries and 2 staged `set_operation` entries (`physicists_who_were_nobel_laureates` and `aau_big_ten_intersection_universities`), totaling 8/8 after this instance. The same scan shows `multi_attribute_projection` already at 2 registered + 6 staged = 8/8, so set_operation is the second saturated category after multi_attribute_projection.
- Preflight: PASS. CSV has 17 rows x 5 columns; `University` primary key is unique; no blank cells; CSV header equals `draft.json::columns`; `source_count = 2 = len(source_urls)`; row count is >= 10; `query_category=set_operation`, `secondary_category=temporal`, and `operation_type=intersect`; `claim_type=source_defined`; CSV is alphabetically sorted by University; `domain=Education/Higher Education` follows the domain taxonomy's preferred `Family/Subdomain` pattern and is not misleading for an AAU/research-university membership intersection.
